item.text:
Using the local prior as the factual base, I only added narrative/attribution sources for office, authority, constraints, and 2022 events. I did not re-fetch the structured country-year facts already supplied.

**Bottom Line**
- In 2022, Nguyễn Phú Trọng was the CPV General Secretary, Secretary of the Central Military Commission, and head of the central anti-corruption apparatus, not president.
- His power came from the CPV’s constitutionally leading role and party control over executive selection, not from a competitive electoral mandate.
- The main inherited constraints in 2022 were the one-party system, tightly managed elections, party-controlled media, weak independent oversight, and an active security apparatus.
- The year combined a strong economic rebound with continued repression and high-profile anti-corruption prosecutions.

**Retained Sources**
| Source | Publisher / Date | Direct URL | What it is useful for | Period fit / ruler attribution | Limits / contrary points |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Constitution of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, Article 4](https://thuvienphapluat.vn/van-ban/EN/Bo-may-hanh-chinh/Constitution-dated-November-28-2013-of-the-socialist-republic-of-Vietnam/221949/tieng-anh.aspx?tab=7) | Thư Viện Pháp Luật / 2013-11-28 | same | Primary legal basis for CPV supremacy and party organs operating within law | Structural backdrop, not 2022-specific; explains why Trọng’s authority is party-based | The text is constitutional self-description; independent reports say the party monopoly is more controlling in practice than the text suggests |
| [Biography of Nguyen Phu Trong, General Secretary of 13th Party Central Committee](https://en.nhandan.vn/biography-of-nguyen-phu-trong-general-secretary-of-13th-party-central-committee-post94682.html) | Nhan Dan / 2021-02-01 | same | Confirms office history: General Secretary, CMC secretary, anti-corruption head, and president only through 2021 | Directly relevant to 2022 office and authority; shows he was still the top party figure in 2022 | State media biography is favorable and sanitizing; independent rights sources give a less flattering picture of his leadership style |
| [Confidently making breakthrough, comprehensively developing the nation: Top leader](https://en.nhandan.vn/confidently-making-breakthrough-comprehensively-developing-the-nation-top-leader-post110354.html) | Nhan Dan / 2022-01-31 | same | Early-2022 self-framing of priorities: recovery, party building, anti-corruption, national defense | Good fit for 2022 agenda-setting and ruler attribution | Self-presentational interview; should not be treated as independent validation |
| [Tổng Bí thư Nguyễn Phú Trọng chúc tết lãnh đạo, nguyên lãnh đạo Đảng, Nhà nước](https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-phat-bieu-cua-tong-bi-thu-nguyen-phu-trong-chuc-tet-lanh-dao-nguyen-lanh-dao-dang-nha-nuoc-mttq-viet-nam-119230120092648062.htm) | Chinhphu.vn / 2023-01-20 | same | Year-end wrap-up of 2022 achievements: stability, growth, security, anti-corruption, social welfare | Directly covers 2022 and shows how the leadership presented the year | Officially curated; independent sources dispute the degree to which gains were matched by political openness |
| [TOÀN VĂN: Kết luận của Tổng Bí thư Nguyễn Phú Trọng tại cuộc họp phòng chống tham nhũng, tiêu cực](https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-ket-luan-cua-tong-bi-thu-nguyen-phu-trong-tai-cuoc-hop-phong-chong-tham-nhung-tieu-cuc-119221118204327577.htm) | Chinhphu.vn / 2022-11-18 | same | Confirms he personally chaired the anti-corruption apparatus and reviewed 2022 case progress | Directly relevant to governance authority and corruption campaign in 2022 | Official framing emphasizes discipline and moral renewal; critics say enforcement is selective and politically filtered |
| [Vietnam 2022 GDP growth quickens to 8.02%, fastest since 1997](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/vietnam-2022-gdp-growth-quickens-to-802-vs-258-expansion-in-2021-2970866) | Reuters / 2022-12-28 | same | Independent macro context: strong post-COVID rebound, export-led growth, but global headwinds | Directly covers 2022 inherited conditions and ruler context | GDP growth does not speak to distribution, governance quality, or rights conditions |
| [Vietnam refutes rumor that prize-winning environmentalist was jailed for climate-related activities](https://news.tuoitre.vn/vietnam-refutes-rumor-that-prize-winning-environmentalist-was-jailed-for-climate-related-activities-10367783.htm) | Tuổi Trẻ / 2022-06-24 | same | Local-language favorable source showing the state’s legal defense of Nguy Thi Khanh’s conviction as tax evasion | Good 2022 case study for official justification and local-language framing | It reflects the government line; HRW, Amnesty, and foreign governments read the case as repression of environmental activism |
| [Nhìn lại Việt Nam năm 2022](https://www.rfa.org/vietnamese/in_depth/looking-back-at-vietnam-2022-12302022091753.html) | RFA Vietnamese / 2022-12-30 | same | Local-language critical year-in-review naming major 2022 events: Việt Á, rescue flights, growth, China relations | Strong for domestic critical framing of the year’s inherited problems | Commentary-heavy, not a primary record; should be paired with documentary and official sources |
| [Vietnam: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/vietnam/freedom-world/2023) | Freedom House / 2023 | same | Clear summary of one-party rule, predetermined top posts, and 2022 corruption and activist crackdowns | Very strong for constraints and political structure affecting 2022 | Index/report format is synthesized rather than event-by-event primary evidence |
| [Vietnam: Crackdown Extends to Activist Groups](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/01/12/vietnam-crackdown-extends-activist-groups) | Human Rights Watch / 2023-01-12 | same | Documents the 2022 escalation against activists, journalists, and environmental defenders | Directly covers 2022 repression and prosecution patterns | Advocacy report; the government denies the political motive of these prosecutions |
| [Vietnam - 2022 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices](https://2021-2025.state.gov/report/custom/3c5ee2c644/) | U.S. Department of State / 2023-03-20 | same | Official U.S. government rights summary: authoritarian one-party state, arbitrary arrests, censorship, assembly limits, corruption | Directly about calendar-year 2022; useful for a broad institutional constraint baseline | A foreign-government report, not a neutral court record; still useful because it is methodical and source-backed |
| [Amnesty International Report 2022/23: Việt Nam](https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/pol10/5670/2023/vi/) | Amnesty International / 2023-03-27 | same | Strong 2022 rights narrative: crackdowns on dissent, digital surveillance, arbitrary detention, and the tightening of civic space | Directly covers 2022 and adds detail on civil space, torture, and climate activists | Advocacy report; should be cross-checked against state responses and Reuters/HRW for event specifics |

**Source Families To Keep**
- Primary official / favorable: Constitution, Nhan Dan biography, Chinhphu speeches, Tuổi Trẻ’s quoted government defense.
- Independent wire / event reporting: Reuters.
- Local-language critical: RFA Vietnamese.
- Rights-monitoring / structural constraint sources: Freedom House, HRW, Amnesty, U.S. State Department.

**Compact Event Map**
- January 2022: Trọng opens the year with a recovery-and-discipline agenda, tying growth to party unity and anti-corruption.
- June 2022: Ngụy Thị Khanh is convicted on tax-evasion charges; officials insist the case is legal, while independent monitors treat it as repression of climate civil society.
- November 2022: Trọng chairs the anti-corruption body and reviews ongoing case handling, showing the campaign remained central to governance.
- December 2022: Vietnam posts 8.02% GDP growth, but this sits alongside continued crackdowns on activists and journalists.
- Late 2022: Domestic critical summaries highlight Việt Á, rescue flights, and other scandals as evidence of deep institutional problems.

**Chapter Source Plan**
- `1B`: keep the chapter empty unless a new nuclear-capability narrative source is needed; the local prior already says no evidence.
- `2B`: use the biography and anti-corruption/defense-adjacent official sources only if a narrative link to military authority is required.
- `3B`: HRW, Amnesty, State Department, Freedom House, and RFA Vietnamese for repression, detention, movement restrictions, and civic-space constraints.
- `4B`: Constitution Article 4, Freedom House, State Department, and HRW for one-party control, no real opposition, and media constraints.
- `5B`: Reuters GDP plus the official New Year/Tet speeches for macro context and leadership framing.
- `6B`: official New Year/Tet speech plus Reuters and State Department for welfare context and recovery claims.
- `7B`: anti-corruption conclusion, HRW, Amnesty, and State Department for the corruption campaign and its selective-enforcement critique.
- `8B`: official self-assessment plus Freedom House, State Department, Reuters, and Amnesty for governance-capacity context.

If you want, I can turn this into a cleaner dossier format next, with one short evidence paragraph per chapter `1B` through `8B` and the source IDs assigned for reuse.
